2607.25038.title: Grounded in Consensus, In Step With Emerging Science: A Consensus-Anchored Multi-Corpus Clinical Chatbot for Long COVID
2607.25038.paper_summary: Long COVID (LC) poses a challenge for clinical decision support because relevant evidence is distributed across sources with different update cycles, evidentiary roles, and levels of clinical maturity. We present a clinician-facing chatbot that organizes four sources within a retrieval-augmented workflow: expert-curated consensus guidance, current PubMed literature, registered interventional trials, and evidence from living systematic reviews. Consensus guidance is always included to frame responses, while the remaining sources are retrieved in parallel when selected by the user. In an exploratory automated evaluation on 50 clinician-facing questions, our chatbot showed comparable mean ratings to OpenEvidence, with numerically higher scores and lower score variability in an LLM-judged comparison.
2607.25038.paper_summary_zh: 長期新冠（LC）對臨床決策支持提出了挑戰，因為相關證據分散在不同更新週期、證據角色和臨床成熟度的來源中。<lb/>我們提出了一個面向臨床醫生的聊天機器人，該機器人在增強檢索的工作流程中組織了四個來源：專家策劃的共識指導、當前的PubMed文獻、登記的介入試驗，以及來自動態系統評價的證據。<lb/>共識指導始終包括在內，以框定回應，而其餘來源則在用戶選擇時並行檢索。<lb/>在對50個面向臨床醫生的問題進行的探索性自動評估中，我們的聊天機器人在平均評分上顯示出與OpenEvidence相當的結果，並在LLM評判比較中具有數值上更高的分數和更低的分數變異性。
